target_customer: Manufacturers (electronics, automotive, food, packaging) buying inspection systems
problem: Factories ship defective products because quality problems are caught late and legacy machine vision is slow and costly to deploy.
business_model: Hardware plus software sales of smart cameras and inspection platform
product_category: AI machine vision for manufacturing quality

founders.name: Austin Appel
education: Northwestern University, BS Manufacturing Engineering and Mechanical Engineering
founders.background_notes: Four years at Tesla in manufacturing and R&D per YC page.

founders.name: Christopher Van Dyke
founders.background_notes: Eight years at Tesla, built the team that designed the Gigafactory and launched Supercharger network per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A small team had to build custom camera hardware, edge deep learning inference and software for factory use, which spans hardware and ML (YC page, company site).

defensibility.rationale: Installed hardware on production lines creates switching costs, but machine vision is a crowded field with established vendors and open ML tooling.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not established from sources opened. No acquisition found; company still independent in 2026 per its site.

market_need_then: Founders came from Tesla manufacturing and say large manufacturers waste billions on quality issues (YC page and description). Specific 2019 spend data not sourced.

branding.domain_note: Operates at overview.ai; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct claims such as Built to Deploy Fast. Built for Zero Missed Defects.
